q: Muscle tissue in anaerobic conditions is treated with a drug that blocks lactate dehydrogenase. Predict the outcome.
options: NADH builds up and NAD+ runs out, so glycolysis stops and ATP production collapses
ATP production rises, because pyruvate is no longer wasted by being turned into lactate
Pyruvate enters the Krebs cycle instead, which keeps ATP production at its normal level
The muscle cells switch to producing ethanol and CO2 to regenerate their NAD+ instead
explanation: Without O2 the electron transport chain can't reoxidise NADH, and with lactate dehydrogenase blocked there is no other route to regenerate NAD+. Triose phosphate oxidation stops, so glycolytic ATP production halts. The Krebs cycle needs NAD+ and a working electron transport chain (O2), and human cells lack the enzymes for ethanol fermentation.
